Cat Bait is a very cute roguelike, and I really enjoyed the first few runs. The charm and presentation carried the experience early on, and it was fun figuring things out at the start. Unfortunately, the repetition started to set in pretty quickly. The game feels very slow-paced, and the limited variety in upgrades, strategies, and gameplay options made later runs feel more tedious than fun. The final achievement felt especially frustrating. It seemed impossible to beat the Sockeye Vessel level on normal difficulty without grinding permanent upgrades through constant replays to collect coins. Maybe part of that is a skill issue on my end, but the slow speed and lack of variety made the grind feel more boring than rewarding. There’s definitely a cute and enjoyable game here, but the long-term replayability just isn't there.

I think the game needs more abilities/passives, which would give the player more ways of creating builds on the fly. It maybe needs some balance tweaking too. Every time I get hit by an enemy, it feels like a huge setback. Also, we should be able to use the special ability of each class more frequently, so that it defines how you play with that character. Instead, the abilities are like a “cooldown” which you never use except for a critical moment. It’s an Early Access game, so I am not giving up on it, but I am putting it aside for now.

This game is bascially a fake roguelike. Once you pick a certain amount of upgrades for a helper you are locked out of the others and there are no unique builds due to that. Some final upgrades are also worse than the base weapon by a lot. You pretty much just choose the same thing every time and the meta upgrades mostly don't matter aside from the ones that let you take more damage or do more damage. Rerolling would be useful except it isn't since the game will just automatically force you to pick a specific upgrade once you start it's path anyways. There are no accessories and there are no characters but rather abilities you swap. Most of the enemies are just reskins but they're more annoying with a few unique ones each level. It's early access but the core of the game is just boring and too easy once you figure out the weapon selection isn't actually random but fixed paths the game just throws at you. You pretty much experienced the entire game if you played the demo. tl;dr This game is more or less a stripped down brotato but without unique character builds or weapons. Really lacking in content and variety with questionable progression. I honestly don't see the inspritation when the outfits don't even have different stats and there are 0 accessory items nor currency to buy things between waves with. There are no perks or traits. As far as survivors-like "bullet heaven" games, Cat Bait is a weaker entry to the genre, but it has just enough charm to earn a positive review. Positives: - The pixel art is cute and has a lot of charm. The "cat and mouse" theme is used to create a lot of fun character and enemy designs. - The music is surprisingly good for the most part. I enjoy the way it ramps up in intensity after several waves have passed. - Each character skin has a different unique ability that, at first, seems superfluous and not particularly useful. However, they can make a big difference in a couple of the more challenging scenarios. - Weapons have powered-up versions that can be accessed after levelling them up a few times. Negatives: - Every "weapon" is actually a helper cat standing atop a pillar just above the arena. These are some of the most fun character designs, yet the only way to see them is by walking to the top of the arena (something you'll rarely be doing organically). It seems odd to me to go through the effort of designing and animating these delightful characters only for them to go mostly completely unseen. - There are only three environments (for the time being). - There aren't very many weapon choices, and even fewer buff options (literally just a minor speed buff that can be chosen once and a dodge buff). - The game doesn't communicate that there are different powered-up versions of the weapons (which I believe are determined by which weapon stat you focused on powering up). - Your character moves quite sluggishly. - I like the idea of using accumulated currency to permanently boost certain stats, but it seems weird to me that the coin drop rate can only be increased ONCE. - Some of the weapons seems exceedingly difficult to use effectively. The falling anvils, for instance, can't be aimed and, if used as a starting weapon, require walking around defensively hoping for them to fall where enemies are. The land mines, as another example, tend to accumulate near the edges of the arena where they aren't particularly useful. - While the store page says the game is "mostly playable" with a controller, I couldn't get it to recognize any controller inputs at all. - The logo reads to me as "Cat Bail". So while it's a bit rough around the edges and needs some more time in the oven, I still ultimately enjoyed Cat Bait, mostly because its charming presentation allowed me to forgive some of its flaws.
